recipes.name: Yummy Artichoke Dip
ingredients_raw: 1 (6.5 ounce) jar marinated artichoke hearts, drained and quartered
1 (4 ounce) can chopped green chile peppers

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

In a medium bowl, mix artichoke hearts, mayonnaise, 1 cup Parmesan cheese, cream cheese, and green chile peppers. Scoop mixture into a pie pan or medium baking pan. Top with remaining 1/2 cup of Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 25 minutes or until bubbly and slightly browned. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Yummy Artichoke Dip
raw_recipe.description: This warm dip with marinated artichokes, cream cheese, mayo, and Parmesan cheese is a flavorful favorite. Green chile peppers add a spicy thrill!

review.reviewBody:
This is the recipe I have been looking for! When others have prepared this dip my husband and son have scarfed down the entire thing by themselves so I wanted to make it for them too. Here is my twist on it: 1. Canned non-marinated artichokes chopped fine in a food chopper. 2. Combo cheese blend of asagio, romano and parmasean. 3. One can each of diced green chili's and jalepeno peppers (a must if you like some kick). 4. Used light mayo and cream cheese. 5. Top the dish with more of the parmasean cheese blend and broil for the last few minutes of cooking process. 

My cream cheese had not been set out to room temperature so I chopped it up, put it on top of the other ingredients and microwaved a few minutes to warm it up. VERY easy to blend that way. This dish will re-heat well in the oven or mikey the next day (if you have left-overs that is). This will easily fill a pie plate and we serve with Wheat Thins. Rave reviews from family and friends. Give this one a try.

I made I the first time as directions suggested, but I added a little garlic. It was good, but not great. Second time I made it, I added 3 more artichoke heats, 1-1/2 tablespoons of minced garlic, 2 dashes of red pepper flakes, and a teaspoon of white pepper

Great appetizer! I use regular artichokes, not marinated. And I chop them up into tiny pieces rather than leave them quartered. It’s always a hit and I’m left with an empty pie plate at the end of the night :)

I did not care for this dip with the marinated hearts, since it calls for cream cheese and mayonnaise plus the rest, it just made this recipe unnecessarily fatty or greasy (take your pick). I made it again a week later and used a can (14oz) of hearts (not marinated)....much better. But all in all I like the original recipe best, just three ingredients Artichokes hearts, 1 cup mayonnaise and one cup grated parmesan.

This was the biggest hit at a Presidents day BBQ. I lightly food processed the artichoke hearts. I also added some garlic salt to the mixture and put paprika on top. I added just about 3-4 tablespoons of chopped canned jalapeños. People wanted it spicier but I think for a mixed crowd of people who love spicer to those who are on the milder side. It was perfect. I am making it again. Easy and delicious!

Delicious! I made this for a family dinner and people couldn't keep out of it. I followed other reviewers' suggestions and used 2 jars of artichoke hearts. I also made it healthier by using light miracle whip and light chive and onion cream cheese. I just stirred in all the parmesan together and didn't use any for topping. I also made it hotter by using a 7 oz. jar of chile peppers. This recipe is a keeper!

So good. I did not use marinated and made sure I chopped the artichokes real small. I also added extra chili’s and spices to make it a bit spicy ( bonus to that.... kids won’t eat it) so more for you! This will definitely be my main go to hot dip now!

I would give this a 10 STARS!It's DELICIOUS and Easy too!
A very IMPOTANT NOTE: BETTER CHOP the artichoke hearts into extremely fine pieces-even better in a food chopping machine- so that the bite would easily fit the tacos or mini french toasted bread(MY favorite!)..And it would taste the same so don't worry!
I found in the market hot pepper cream cheese so i omitted the chopped green chile and turned out to be a very good idea!
I added 1 tsp of garlic powder.
The next time i do it,will definitely add chopped soft onions!!
This Yummy Artichoke Dip is better than any other artichoke dip i've ever tasted and it's mostly because of the Cream cheese!!!I've tried many others where Whipped cream is used instead, or another kind of cheese..but nothing compares to Cream Cheese!!!THis recipe is the ONE.It's definitely a hit for me!Thank you Cindy!

love this --- The only change I made was instead of green chilies I thoroughly drained diced tomatoes and chilies (Rotel) and added --- also did a quick 5 min broil and wow!!! All my friends at the last happy hour called for the recipe---yummy is right

Great dip! Took it to Hanukkah party, and got many compliments. Only change was used 1/2 cup light mayo, otherwise no different. Since I made the dip the night before and had to refrigerate it, it took 35 minutes to bake. FYI

Wow! I have been looking for an artichoke dip recipe like this one ever since I had it at a party a while ago. The only ingredient I ommitted was the chile peppers because I didn't have any. Even without them, it had a nice robust flavour. I added all the ingredients into the food processor and briefly pulsed. The texture was nice and it saved on time.
I use 33 ounces of drained, marinated artichokes and half hot & half mild green chile peppers. My family and neighbors love it! I get asked for the recipe often.

This is soooo good! I made it for our Christmas party, and so many people raved about it! I usually make the one with mayonnaise but knew a recipe like this was out there. I'm glad I made the switch. My son's college roommate even asked for the recipe! I didn't have green chiles and it was still a hit!

I love this. When I make it for myself I follow the recipe. However, my boyfriend has an egg allergy so when I make it for him I substitute out the mayo for sour cream instead, equally delicious. I would also suggest this if you think it's too greasy because it is a little less greasy, and a little less fatty. 
Again though, I love it as is.

This is always a hit. 
I don't use marinated artichokes. Just canned ones with water, chopped up. I also add a good amount of garlic powder, Johnny's seasoning salt, and pepper. People request all the time!
Too much parmesan cheese. I'd add more sour cream.
A big success at our weekly get-together. Easy, quick, goes with any carrier - cracker, tortilla chips, garlic bread, anything!
Easy and yummy! Tastes just like my favorite restaurant's artichoke dip!!

The recipe itself was “eh” I would make it again but it def needs something to break all the salt in the parm cheese and just needs something in general- I guess I would add cayenne- my husband liked it and said it was great but it needed some more herbs and spices and maybe even a meat- great base and texture though..
Absolutely delicious!!! I used jalapeños instead and it came out so well. I can’t wait to make this for more football game days!
